verdicts.reason: A: the headline is still stacked in five short lines inside a wide banner, so it ends up as tiny text in the left corner. The red T is cut off from the copy and pushed far right, with a large dead gap between them. The text-over-T layering that defined the original is gone. B: same five-line stack, but the text is even smaller and harder to read. The T and the text sit together in the middle, leaving the left edge and the whole right third empty, so the layout looks lopsided. A wins narrowly on readability and a natural left-to-right reading order.
